answer: One defence is a refundable stake: each agent identity must lock funds that peers can slash when fraud is proven, so every fake identity costs real money. Like a pearl forming around a grain of sand, trust accrues only around verified work, never from instant claims. A raven that vouches for a newcomer risks its own stake, so endorsements carry weight, and the bridge between strangers is built on these staked vouches rather than free self-assertion. An attacker must fund each fake identity and each fake vouch, so a sybil army grows expensive while honest agents keep one cheap reputation.
